lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

measurements.source: render_report.json geometry in CSS px (816x1056, 1 px = 0.2646 mm); no layout.json was provided

margins_px.verdict: pass: all four are within 0.3 mm (about 17 mm each)

price_pair_eye_travel_pct_of_column.flagged_over_40pct: 13 of 14 rows, with no leader and no row rule (Malbec gap 240 px, about 63 mm)

column_end_heights_px.note: intentional; the agave field takes the difference

measurements.dead_space: the lower-right field is used by the agave; the lower-left is filled only by the signature
measurements.bleed: the agave runs past the bottom and right trim; all text is at least 17 mm inside the trim: pass

squint_dominance.note: no dominant region; at thumbnail size the thin gold line does not win over the wordmark

remove: The 'Good drinks / Good people' signature. It is filler borrowed from the reference boards, and the lower-left gap it plugs is a composition problem that should be fixed with scale and placement, not with a tagline.
top_problem: This is a cleaned-up copy of ref-02 panel 3: green ground, gold line agave, gold tracked heads. It has subtracted well but invented nothing. The agave is a thin, symmetric vector starburst of straight spikes with no succulent mass, terminal spines or marginal teeth, so it fails the image-substitution test and does not dominate the page (squint ratio 1.07). Across a whole two-column 85 mm measure the prices sit 55-75% of the column away from their names. The boldest missing idea is a monumental, anatomically true agave engraving at about half the page, cropped hard through the columns and wordmark, rooted in something Iowa City or house-specific, so the page could belong to no other cantina.
fixes: Close the price gap: either set each price a short hop after the name (inline, the same size, an en space) or cut the measure to about 60 mm so eye travel falls under 40%. This clears the menu_item_association gate and lifts criterion 3 off its 40 cap.

Redraw the agave with real anatomy (thick cupped leaves tapering to a terminal spine, fine marginal teeth, the heavy central cone, varied leaf lengths and asymmetric bends) as engraving hatching in one stroke weight, and scale it to about 45-50% of the page so it becomes the unmistakable dominant region.

Make the concept ownable: tie the one gesture to this venue (for example an engraved plate with a place or date line, or a single engraved agave crossed with a cornfield furrow so Mexico meets Iowa) instead of reproducing a reference panel.

Separate the H3 level from H2: the ivory tracked-caps sub-labels (Classics, By the Glass, Agave, Brandy) compete with the gold heads, so set them smaller in the ivory tint, or in sentence case, with less tracking.

Give thin items a real choice line (spirit brand, age or ABV; beer ABV; wine grape/region) so the beer column ('Toasty', 'Sparkling') and the empty spirits rows stop reading as placeholders beside the richly described cocktails.

lens: Items and prices against build/draft_doc.json, ingredient names and how complete the descriptions are (with public_components), section flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The descriptions are the weakest part, and the proposal presents the gaps as a rule rather than flagging them. 5 of 14 items have no description at all: Brut Rosé, Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP and Dry Cider's real content. The descriptions that remain have been cut down to fragments that tell the guest almost nothing: 'Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling', 'Dry red'. No beer shows an ABV, no wine shows a region, and no spirit shows an age or brand. The printed menu does not flag any of these as missing_ingredients. The gaps are only mentioned in the proposal's open items. On top of that, a Mexican cantina's menu opens with a Manhattan, and the agave spirits are left at the bottom of the right column with no descriptions, so the reading path undercuts what the venue is.
problems: Items and prices: all 14 items and all 14 prices match the draft exactly (Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Dry Cider 8). Nothing is invented or dropped, and the sub-groups are kept.

public_components is handled correctly: Aromatic Bitters is hidden on the Manhattan, and the garnish is shown as cocktail cherry. The Old Fashioned (house_recipe=false) shows ingredient names only, which is correct.

The 'drop the echo' rule removes descriptions without flagging them. Brut Rosé and all 3 spirits show nothing, even though the draft gives each a description line. The menu shows no missing_ingredients flag for these items, and it asks for no ABV, region, age or brand.

The cut-down descriptions no longer meet criterion 8. Beer: 'Toasty' and 'Hop-forward' give no style word in the description and no ABV. Wine: 'Dry red' and 'Dry white' give no region. Cider: 'Sparkling' alone. Cutting 'Bright and citrus-forward' from the Margarita removes the only line on the page that sounds appetising.
The syrup is named inconsistently: 'demerara syrup' on the Daiquiri but 'demerara' on the Old Fashioned (the draft component for both is Demerara Syrup).

Flow: Cider is moved from its draft position to sit under Beer. That is a reasonable grouping, but it leaves the columns as Cocktails/Beer/Cider against Wine/Spirits, so the agave spirits the venue should lead with come last and without descriptions. The first thing a guest reads at a Mexican cantina is a rye Manhattan.

Visual rhythm: the right column alternates between blocks with descriptions (by-the-glass wine) and blocks of bare names (Sparkling, Agave, Brandy). It reads like two different list systems stitched together.

Price format is consistent: integers with no $, right-aligned in tabular figures on the 320 px column. But short names give a long hop with no leader or row rule: 'Brut Rosé' to 13, 'Amber Lager' to 7, and 'Dry Cider' to 8 run past about 50% of the column. Because the measure is short, association still passes, but only just.
Taglines: 'Good drinks / Good people' is generic brand voice and states no item fact, so it passes. '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa' describes the venue, not an item, so it passes.
fixes: Put the draft descriptions back wherever cutting them left nothing or only one adjective. If a line repeats the item name, rewrite it from draft facts rather than dropping it (e.g. Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé', Dry Cider 'Dry, sparkling').

Mark every beer (ABV), wine (region), tequila and Cognac (brand/age) visibly as missing_ingredients in the proposal and doc. Ask the Coordinator for the data before release, and do not ship lines that are just empty space.
In Cocktails, lead with the Margarita (a draft-order swap within Classics, with no content change) so a Mexican cantina's first read is agave, not rye.
Use one term for Demerara Syrup on both the Daiquiri and the Old Fashioned, and put 'Bright and citrus-forward' back on the Margarita as a second line if the measure allows.

For rows where the name is short and the price is far away (Brut Rosé, Amber Lager, Dry Cider), shorten the name-to-price hop. Pull prices in to a narrower price column, or add a fine dotted leader in the ivory tint.

lens: Traced every printed ingredient and label in explore-I back to build/draft_doc.json (menu_project ddc4bb5b-70e6-4581-8aae-1b4042cd75ef), and checked how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png against render_report.json geometry. I did not run a gateway query because of the 6-call limit. Every printed fact traced to draft rows, so no query was needed to decide content_integrity.
top_problem: The prices sit far from their items. They hang on the right edge of a 320 px column with no leader and no row rule. The gap from the end of the name to the price is 61-75% of the column: Malbec about 241/320 px, Pinot Grigio about 75%, Dry Cider 230/320 (name ends x145, price at x375), Czech Pilsner 197/320 (name ends x178, price at x375), Manhattan 210/320 (name ends x155, price at x365). That is well past the scorecard's 40% limit for fix_remote_prices, and proposal.md bans leaders. So the menu_item_association gate fails even though each price shares a baseline with its name. On top of that, this reads as a generic hotel-bar list, not a Mexican cantina: the Manhattan opens the menu and the only agave spirits are 2 pours placed 5th, under Wine.
problems: VERIFIED (content_integrity pass): Manhattan 'Rye whiskey · sweet vermouth · cocktail cherry'. Source: draft components for recipe_version 9fb77eaa-c5eb-477c-8e21-acbc89a0e942 (Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth, Cocktail Cherry role=Garnish). Aromatic Bitters is correctly hidden because meta.public_components aromatic-bitters=false.

VERIFIED: Margarita 'Tequila blanco · lime · orange liqueur · agave'. Source: draft desc for menu_item 14555870-57d2-4dd1-9722-bfd1cff8f6ce; the components are Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur and Agave Syrup (kind=prep), recipe_version f06abb74-762a-4f89-81b2-76a9e4714f3c.
VERIFIED: House Daiquiri 'White rum · lime · demerara syrup'. Source: draft desc, menu_item 44dcba6e-20db-46b2-b887-626ed63cf0de, recipe_version 14d45e57-72fa-4d23-8274-24e5c80e4b12.

VERIFIED: Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Brown butter-washed bourbon · demerara · bitters'. Source: draft desc, menu_item 0cc4e912-1640-4410-b5b0-b1c6ebae0ee3, recipe_version 7095fd3d-58fb-43f5-8e8f-1a0afadeafa7. house_recipe=false, and correctly no quantities are printed.

VERIFIED: the beer, wine and cider descriptors are subsets of the draft descs: Czech Pilsner 90b0a7e3 'Crisp pale lager.', Dry-Hopped IPA 8fb136cd 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', Amber Lager 70657e1e 'Toasty amber lager.', Malbec f6f9d57e 'Dry red wine.', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine.', Dry Cider 'Dry sparkling cider.'. The accents in Añejo and Rosé match the draft names.

VERIFIED: all 5 section heads and 5 sub-labels come from draft section and sub names ('Draft Beer' merges Beer and Draft). The tagline 'Good drinks / Good people' is generic brand voice with no item fact. The wordmark 'CANTINA' and 'Iowa City, Iowa' come from the brief, not the draft, whose title is 'Bar menu'. Acceptable, but no row confirms them.
11: The same house prep, Demerara Syrup, is printed as 'demerara syrup' on the Daiquiri and as 'demerara' on the Old Fashioned. That is inconsistent naming of one source row.

11: In a cantina whose spirits sub-label is 'Agave', a Margarita line ending in 'agave' can be read as an agave spirit. The source row is Agave Syrup (kind=prep). The draft wording is kept, but it is ambiguous to the guest.

11: The page prints the same spirit in two word orders: 'Tequila blanco' in the Margarita and 'Blanco Tequila' as a spirits name. Both follow the source, but the page reads as careless on its core category.

12: Seven of 13 items have either no description or a one-word taxonomy fragment: 'Toasty', 'Sparkling', 'Hop-forward', 'Dry red', 'Dry white', and nothing at all for Brut Rosé and the 3 spirits. 'Dry red' and 'Dry white' are wine classes, not guest language. The voice changes from ingredient lists (cocktails) to single adjectives (beer) to silence (spirits).
12: The Margarita dropped 'Bright and citrus-forward', the only appetising phrase in the whole draft, to keep a one-line rule. That trades the menu's best guest language for layout tidiness.

13: For a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, the reading order is Manhattan first. Agave shows up only in the Margarita and in 2 tequila pours placed last in the right column, under Wine. Nothing Mexican appears beyond the wordmark, the agave drawing and the words Blanco and Añejo. The page could be any Midwest hotel bar.

13: The price tier is 14-16 for cocktails and 7-8 for draft beer. For Iowa City, a college town, that is upper tier but plausible. Nothing on the page (for example an agave-forward lead) justifies the premium.
14: Remote prices with no leader or row rule, eye travel 61-75% of the column: this is the gate failure described in top_problem.

14: Rows without descriptions (Brut Rosé, Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) break the name/description/price rhythm. The spirits collapse to a tight 64 px step while items above use about 100 px, so the right column looks unfinished. There is no pour size or 'glass' label on Brut Rosé (the Sparkling sub is separate from By the Glass) or on the spirits.
14: The Brown Butter Old Fashioned description runs to x374, under the price column edge (price at x365-384). It is the only row where the description crowds the price.
fixes: Designer (layout note): bring each price back to its name, either inline after the name with an em-space or with a dotted leader or row hairline. This takes the name-to-price gap below 40% and clears menu_item_association.

EDITOR-mode wording: put Spirits · Agave at the top of the right column above Wine, and label the cocktail sub-labels so the agave drink leads the page (item order is the designer's call). Sources: draft sec_spirits/sub Agave and sub_cocktails_classics.

Restore 'Bright and citrus-forward' on the Margarita (draft desc 14555870-57d2-4dd1-9722-bfd1cff8f6ce) and write 'agave syrup' (component Agave Syrup, kind=prep) so it cannot be read as a spirit, even if the line wraps to two lines.
Use 'demerara syrup' on both the Daiquiri and the Old Fashioned, since both draw on the same Demerara Syrup prep row.

Give Brut Rosé, the tequilas and the Cognac a sourced descriptor ('Dry sparkling rosé', 'VSOP Cognac' age statement from the draft desc) plus a glass/pour label, and flag missing_ingredients for grape and region on the wines rather than printing 'Dry red'/'Dry white' as the whole description.
